In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

(Tafsir of) Surah Maryam, Meccan.

(And) we have related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Surat Bani Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam and Ta-Ha are of my old possessions (taladi)." In another narration: "They are from the first of the old (al-'ataq al-awwal)."

As for the words of the Most High, ﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ain, Sad﴾. It is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "This is one of the names of Allah the Most High." It is also reported from him that he said: "O Allah, O 'Ain, Sad, forgive me." From al-Hasan and Qatadah: it is one of the names of the surah. As for Ibn 'Abbas, what is narrated from him is that each letter is taken from a name: the Kaf is taken from al-Kafi (the Sufficient); some said it is from Kabir (the Great), and some said from Karim (the Generous). As for the Ha, Ibn 'Abbas said: it is taken from al-Hadi (the Guide). As for the Ya, it is taken from Halim (the Forbearing); some said from Yamin (the Oath-Keeper/Right-hand), and some said from Amin (the Trustworthy). Some of them said: the Ya is the Ya of the vocative (ya' al-nida'). As for the 'Ain, Ibn 'Abbas said: from 'Alim (the All-Knowing), and from others: from 'Aziz (the Mighty). As for the Sad, Ibn 'Abbas said: from Sadiq (the Truthful), and some said: from al-Sadim (the Overpowering). We have already mentioned earlier several opinions concerning the disjointed letters at the beginnings of the surahs.

"And His saying: ﴿This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya﴾, meaning: this is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya. Some of them said: in the verse there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir); meaning: this is a mention of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya with mercy."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿When he called upon his Lord with a secret call﴾, that is: he supplicated his Lord with a hidden supplication. And in some reports: "The best supplication is the hidden one, and the best provision is that which suffices." And in some reports also: "The supplication in secret surpasses the supplication openly by seventy degrees."

If it is asked: Why was it hidden? The answer has several aspects. The first: that it is more excellent. The second: that he was shy before the people to supplicate openly, lest they say: "Look at this old man, asking for a child in his old age!" And it is said: it was hidden because he supplicated in the depth of the night while he was prostrating.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 4:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white hair."﴾ He means: they became thin and frail from old age. Qatadah said: he complained of the loss of his molar teeth.

His words: ﴿and my head has filled with white hair﴾, meaning: the hair of the head. The Arabs say, when white hair becomes abundant on the head: "his head has ignited" (ishtaʿala raʾsuh), and this is the finest metaphor, because it ignites in the way fire ignites in firewood.

And His words: ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾ have two interpretations. The first: You have accustomed me to being answered, and You have never disappointed me. The second: "and I have never been unblessed in my supplication" means: when You called me to faith, I believed, and I did not become wretched by abandoning faith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾. Abu Salih said: what is meant by it is the kalalah (collateral heirs). And it is narrated from Abu 'Ubayda: the paternal cousins (banu al-'amm).

And His saying: ﴿after me﴾ means behind me (wara'i ay ba'di). Abu 'Ubayda said: wara'i means in front of me (amami). The first view is more correct.

And in the shadh (irregular reading): "wa-inni khiftu al-mawali min wara'i," meaning: qultu (I said).

And His saying: ﴿And my wife has been barren﴾. The 'aqir (barren woman) is the one who does not bear children.

And His saying: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 6:

And His words, ﴿who shall inherit me﴾, meaning: a son who shall inherit me. If it is said: how could the Prophet of Allah fear that his cousins and male relatives (ʿaṣabah) would inherit from him? And what is the meaning of this fear? It is related from Qatadah that he said: "What concern was there for the Prophet of Allah Zakariyya that anyone other than his own son should inherit from him?"

The answer: opinions differ regarding the inheritance. From Ibn ʿAbbas: he meant inheritance of wealth, and this is the view of a group. Also from him: the intended meaning is inheritance of knowledge, and this is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri. There is a third view: that it is the inheritance of the office of ḥabr (scholar-chief), for he was the head of the rabbis (aḥbār).

Al-Zajjaj said: "The more apt interpretation is that it refers to inheritance other than wealth, because it is unlikely that Zakariyya, peace be upon him, who was one of the prophets, would be concerned that his cousins and male relatives would inherit wealth from him." And it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Zakariyya was a carpenter." The Shaykh, the Imam, the Most Eminent, said: We were informed of it by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Naqur, who said: Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababa said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Baghawi said: Hadbah ibn Khalid related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ)... the report. It was transmitted by Muslim in the Sahih, but al-Bukhari did not transmit it, because it is not narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah [by him].

The meaning of the fear is that he wished that his heir in prophethood and the office of ḥabr would be his son. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three... and he mentioned among them: a righteous child who prays for him."

As for His words, ﴿and inherit from the family of Yaʿqub﴾: it is said that this means prophethood, and it is said that it means kingship, because Zakariyya was of a royal house.

As for His words, ﴿and make him, my Lord, one who is pleasing﴾: meaning, one who is approved (marḍiyyan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 7:

The words of God, Exalted: ﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy﴾ mean: We said, "Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings."

And His words: ﴿a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made for him any namesake before﴾ mean: no one previously was named with his name. If it is said: what virtue does he have in this? We say: the virtue of distinction (takhsis). It was also said: the virtue lies in God's naming him with this name. There is another view on the verse: that His words ﴿We have not made for him any namesake before﴾ mean: no equal or like. For he never sinned, nor did he intend a sin, whereas there is no one who has not sinned or intended a sin. This has been related from the Prophet in a hadith with a continuous chain (musnad) that he said: "No one comes before God on the Day of Resurrection who has not sinned or intended a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya," and then he took a small stick from the ground and said: "He had no more than the like of this." The hadith is gharib (rare).

It was also said, in preventing the suspicion (of a namesake), that no barren woman among women ever bore one like him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 8:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?"﴾ Meaning: [in] despair and dryness (jufuf), as if he complained of the frailty of the bone and the decline of virility.

Ibn Mas'ud recited "ʿasiyan" with the letter sin (ʿisiyan, عسيا), and the meaning is one and the same.

It has been said: How did he ask Allah for a child, and then, when he was answered, say, "How can I have a boy?"

The answer to this is in two respects. The first: he said it in the state of youth, and then he was answered in the state of old age. This view is weak.

The second view: its meaning is, "How can I have a boy?" That is, how can a boy be mine? Will You return me to the state of youth, or grant me a boy while I am an old man? It has also been said that he asked for a child in general, not from this woman, so he said: How can a boy be mine? From this wife or from another?

The Exalted's saying: ﴿He said, "So it is. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me.'"﴾ That is: easy.

And His saying: ﴿"And I created you before, when you were nothing."﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Lord, appoint for me a sign﴾, meaning: a proof (dalalah). If it is said: Why did he ask for a sign? Did God not already confirm the matter, that he should ask for a sign? The answer: in the account, Satan appeared to him and said: "The one who addresses you is not God; rather, it is a devil mocking you." At that point he asked God for a sign, and he asked for the sign in order to increase the tranquility of his heart.

And His saying: ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound﴾, meaning: consecutive. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, and its meaning is: that the people will not speak to you for three nights, while you are sound, with no affliction upon you.

In the account: he was unable to speak with the people, and whenever he wished to glorify God and mention Him, his tongue would be released.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 11:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So he came out to his people from the mihrab (the prayer niche or sanctuary chamber)﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of the mihrab.

And His words: ﴿Then he signalled to them﴾ — that is, he gestured to them, ﴿that you should glorify [Allah] morning and evening.﴾

It is narrated that he would go around to the rabbis every morning and evening, commanding them to worship and to pray. But when these days came, he began to gesture, and it is said that he wrote, so that they read from it.

Some of the scholars said: his tongue being restrained from speech was a punishment upon him, because he asked Allah, the Most High, for a sign after he had heard Allah's promise to him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 19, verse 12:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O Yahya﴾. It is said that Yahya is derived from the saying "yā ḥayy" (O living one). Al-Naqqash related in his tafsir that Sarah's name was originally "Yasarah," and Jibril named her "Sarah." She said, "Why have you reduced a letter from my name?" He said, "It is for a son you will have after you." The name Yahya was "Hayy" in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in the sense that he is alive from two elderly people who had despaired of having a child; then the letter ya' was added to it, and it became "Yahya." In the verse there is an omission, and its meaning is: We gave him a son, then We said: "O Yahya."

And His saying: ﴿Take the Book with strength﴾, that is, with earnestness and diligence.

And His saying: ﴿And We gave him judgment while he was a child﴾, that is, prophethood. This is the view of most of the commentators. Qatadah said: he was given prophethood when he was three years old. It is also said that what is meant by judgment (ḥukm) is knowledge, so he read the Torah while he was young. One of the early scholars said: whoever recites the Qur'an before reaching maturity is among those who were given judgment as a child. There is a third view in the verse, related by Abu Wa'il: that Yahya, while he was a child, was told, "Come, let us play," and he said, "I was not created for play." This is the meaning of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him judgment while he was a child﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 13:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And compassion (ḥanān) from Us﴾, meaning: mercy from Us. The poet said:

(Abā Mundhir, you have spent [us], so let some of us be spared;
Ḥanānayka, some evil is easier than some [other] evil.)

It is derived from taḥannun (tenderness), which is ta'aṭṭuf (kindness, compassion).

And His saying: "and purity (zakāh)" means "purity and divine guidance (tawfīq)." It was also said: sincerity (ikhlāṣ).

And His saying: ﴿and he was devout (taqiyyan)﴾. He described him as having taqwa (God-consciousness) because he had not committed a sin and had not even intended a sin.

And His saying: ﴿and dutiful to his parents﴾, meaning عطوفا (kind and tender).

And His saying: ﴿and was not arrogant, disobedient﴾. الْجَبَّار is the one who kills upon

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And peace is upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾. He singled out these states for these things, because these states are the most frightening of things. For at birth he comes out of his mother's womb in great terror, and he dies in great terror, and he is raised in great terror. The meaning of peace (salam) here is: safety (al-aman) in these situations.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 16:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her family﴾. That is: she withdrew and isolated herself. His words: ﴿from her family﴾, that is: from her people.

His words: ﴿to an eastern place﴾, that is: from the direction of the east. And it is said: it was a day of winter, extremely cold, so she went to its eastern side, delousing her head. And it is narrated that she had just become clean from menstruation, so she went to bathe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 17:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So she took a screen apart from them﴾. Opinions differ regarding this screen (ḥijāb). One view is that it was behind a wall. It was also said that it was behind a mountain. A third view is that it was behind a curtain. It is narrated that she had stripped off her clothes in order to bathe.

His saying: ﴿Then We sent to her Our Spirit﴾. The majority hold that it is Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him. There is another view: that the intended "Spirit" is ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon him, who came in the form of a human being, and she conceived him. The sound position is the first view.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So he appeared before her as a perfect man﴾. In the narrative: he was Jibril, who came in the form of a beardless youth with a handsome face, (having) curly, tightly coiled hair.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿She said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ That is: I seek protection (istijarah) in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing. If it is said: one seeks refuge in the Most Merciful only from a person who is wicked (fajir); but when he is God-fearing (muttaqi), he is not a target of seeking refuge from him, because the God-fearing does not proceed to wickedness. The answer to this: it is like the saying of one who says, "If you are a believer, do not wrong me," meaning that your faith should be a barrier against wronging. Likewise here, the meaning is: your piety should be a barrier against wickedness. It has also been said: she doubted his condition, so she spoke on the basis of doubt. A third view: "if you are God-fearing" means: if you were God-fearing, you would not have come to me in this state. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son..."﴾ (43:81), meaning: the Most Merciful had no son. It is related from one of the early Muslims (salaf) that he said: "If you are God-fearing, know that piety has restraint (dhu nahyah)," meaning: possessed of intellect? For this reason she said: "if you are God-fearing."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 19:

The words of the Most High: ﴿He said, "I am only a messenger from your Lord, to grant you a pure boy."﴾ It was also read as "ليهب لك" (liyahaba laka, "that He may grant you"). So his saying ﴿لأهب﴾ (li-ahaba, "to grant") is attributed to himself, because he was sent with the gift to be delivered through his hand. And his saying "ليهب" (liyahaba) means: "that Allah may grant you." And His saying ﴿غلاما زكيا﴾ (ghulaman zakiyya, "a pure boy") means: pure and righteous.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 20:

His saying: ﴿She said: "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?"﴾ That is: [no] husband. ﴿Nor have I been unchaste﴾ That is: an adulteress (baghiyy). Its meaning: a child comes either from marriage (nikah) or from illicit intercourse (sifah), and neither of these exists here.

"His word, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "So it will be. Your Lord said, 'It is easy for Me.'"﴾ That is: easy (yasir).

And His word: ﴿And We will make him a sign for the people﴾ That is: a sign (ʿalama) for the people and an indication (dalala).

His word: ﴿and as a mercy from Us﴾ That is: and a blessing (niʿma) from Us.

And His word: ﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾ That is: decided (mahkum) and [certain (muhattam)], which cannot be reversed or changed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So she conceived him﴾. In the narrative (al-qissa): Jibril, peace be upon him, blew into the opening of her garment's collar (jayb dir'iha). In another report: into the sleeve of her shirt (kumm qamisiha). In another report: into her mouth (fiha). So she conceived ʿIsa at once, and he began to move in the womb.

And His saying: ﴿So she withdrew with him﴾, meaning she drew apart and went away, ﴿to a remote place﴾, meaning far away and distant.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: the conception and the birth happened in one hour.

Another said: she carried him for eight months, and she gave birth to him, and no child in the world lives if born at eight months. This was a miracle (muʿjiza) for ʿIsa.

In the narrative about Maryam, it is reported that she said: "When I was alone, ʿIsa would speak to me, and I would speak to him while he was in my belly. And when I was with the people and spoke with them, he began to glorify God (yusabbih), and I would hear his glorification."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 23:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree﴾. The people of lexicography (ahl al-lughah) said: jā'ahā (جاءها) and ajā'ahā (أجاءها) have the same meaning, as one says: adhhabtuhu (أذهبته) and dhahabtu bihi (ذهبت به). Mujahid said: fa-ajā'ahā means fa-alja'ahā, i.e., "drove her" or "compelled her." In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "fa-adāhā al-makhāḍ ilā jidh'i al-nakhlah" (﴿the pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree﴾). In some readings it is fājā'ahā (فاجأها), from al-mufājā'ah (suddenness), and the poet said:

(And a neighbour who walked leaning upon you... there came upon him fear and hope)

Al-makhāḍ (المخاض) is the pain of labour. If someone asks: why did she seek refuge at the trunk of the palm tree? The answer is: so that she could shelter under it. The more correct view is that she sought refuge at the palm tree so that she could lean on it, or hold on to it, and thereby be helped in bearing the pain of labour. The evidence that this view is more correct, or that it is well known, is that the palm tree was dry, without a top; and it was said: it was hollow and decayed, and such a tree cannot provide shade. The second view is the correct one. Concerning al-Suddi, he said: the palm tree was dry, but when she shook the palm tree it came to life, bore leaves, and put forth spathes; then the spathes became unripe dates, then ripened, then turned soft, and they fell upon her.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿She said, "Would that I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten, completely forgotten."﴾ Al-nisy (النسي) in the language is that which, when thrown away, is not mentioned and is forgotten, because of its insignificance and baseness. His words "nisyan" mean "abandoned." From Ibn 'Abbas, he said: its meaning is: "Would that I had not been created, and had not been anything at all." From Qatadah: "I would not be known and would not be remembered." From Mujahid, he said: "a blood-clot of a menstrual discharge thrown away."

If it is asked: why did she wish for death? The answer: she wished for death out of shame before her people. It is also said: she wished for death because she knew that people would disbelieve on account of her son and because of her, so she wished for death so that God would not be disobeyed on account of her and on account of her son.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 24:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then he called her from beneath her﴾. It is recited with "min" (from/who) read with a fatha and also with a kasra. As for the one who reads it with a fatha, he takes the verse to mean that the one calling was Jibril (Gabriel). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and a group of others. As for the one who reads it with a kasra, he takes it to mean that the one calling was 'Isa ('Isa, Jesus). This is the view of al-Hasan and Mujahid. The more apparent of the two opinions is that the one calling was Jibril, and it is permissible to interpret both recitations accordingly.

In the narrative: Maryam was on a mound, and Jibril was behind the mound beneath her.

And His saying: ﴿Do not grieve﴾. Do not be distressed by the birth without a husband and by the loneliness.

And His saying: ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that the sarri (stream) here is the river, and it is called sarri because water flows (yasri) in it. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is a small river.

In the narrative: there was there a dry river, and Allah Exalted caused water to flow in it. The evidence for the soundness of this view is that Allah Exalted said in another verse: ﴿So eat and drink﴾, meaning: eat from the fresh dates and drink from the river. The poet also said, using sarri in the sense of river:

(Sahl al-khalifah majid dhu na'il ... mithl al-sarri 'iddat al-anhar)

There is another view regarding sarri, which is that it means: the noble one, and the intended referent is 'Isa. Some of the later scholars said: (Indeed the sarri, when he travels by himself ... and the son of the sarri, when he travels, makes them both travel)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 25:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree﴾ — We have already explained this earlier, and we mentioned that it shook, came into leaf, and bore fruit.

And His words: ﴿It will drop upon you fresh ripe dates﴾ — meaning: it will be dropping (tatasaqqatu). So one of the two tā' letters was assimilated into the other (idgham).

And al-janiyy (the ripe): it is that which has reached its utmost stage and the time for its picking has come.

Al-Kalbi said: "Ruṭaban (fresh ripe dates) with its pollen (bi-ghubārihi)." And it is reported from Ibn al-Musayyib ibn Dārim, who said: "It was barniyy, which is the most satisfying of dates." And it is reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "It was 'ajwah."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 26:

The Most High's words: ﴿So eat and drink﴾, meaning: eat from the fresh dates, and drink from the river.

And His words: ﴿And cool your eye﴾, meaning: be content in your soul. From this is the saying of people: "May God cool your eye" (aqarra Allahu 'aynaka). It is also said that when the eye weeps out of joy, its tears are cool, and when it weeps out of sorrow, its tears are hot; hence "May God cool your eye" and "May God heat his eye."

His words: ﴿And if you see﴾, its meaning: "if you see," and the mention of the nun (in tarayinna) is for emphasis.

His words: ﴿any human being﴾, its meaning is known.

His words: ﴿Then say, "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾. It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading as "samtan" (silence). The well-known reading is "sawman" (fast), and its meaning is silence (samt). It is said that she fasted from speech and food together. It is also said that when a man from the Children of Israel strove hard in worship, he would fast from speech and food together.

A vow (nadhr) is a binding commitment to an act of piety, should a matter be accomplished.

His words: ﴿So I will not speak today to any human being﴾, meaning: to anyone. If it is said: she spoke with these words, so how could she be fasting from speech?

We say: She was permitted this small amount of speech.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 27:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. In the narrative, she gave birth and then immediately (carried him) to her people. In some reports, she brought him to her people forty days after her delivery.

And His words: ﴿They said, "O Maryam, you have certainly come up with something monstrous."﴾ Mujahid said: "Great and objectionable." Abu 'Ubayda said: "Marvelous." It has also been said: "Fabricated, invented." It is related that when she brought 'Isa (ʿĪsā, Jesus) to her people and her household, they grieved greatly—and they were a righteous household—and they entertained suspicions about her.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾ meaning: O likeness of Aaron. Qatadah said: Aaron was a worshipful man among the Children of Israel, and he was not Aaron the brother of Moses. So they likened her to him, meaning: "We thought and assumed that you were in righteousness like Aaron." This is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils﴾, meaning: likenesses of the devils.

And it is related from Ka'b that Aaron was among the most devout and exemplary of the Children of Israel. He said: When he died, forty thousand people prayed over his funeral, all of them named Aaron, apart from the rest of the people, and they used to name their sons after him out of their love for him.

Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to Najran, the Christians of Najran said to him: "You recite: ﴿O sister of Aaron!﴾ Between Mary and Aaron there are such-and-such years." Al-Mughirah did not know how to answer. When he returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, he said: "Why did you not tell them: They used to name themselves after their prophets and righteous people?" Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that by Aaron is meant the brother of Moses, and this is like the speaker saying: "O brother of Tamim," or "O brother of Tha'labah," when he is one of their descendants. Mary was indeed a descendant of Aaron.

A third opinion: that Aaron was a wicked man among the Children of Israel, of great immorality, and so they likened her to him.

A fourth opinion regarding the verse: that Aaron was the full brother of Mary's father, so according to this the meaning of "brotherhood" is kinship by lineage.

As for His saying: ﴿Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, meaning: a fornicator (baghiyy). Its meaning is: how have you come with a grave sin, a fornicator, from two righteous parents?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So she pointed to him﴾ means: so she pointed to him, that is, speak to him. Ibn Mas'ud said: Since she had no proof, she pointed to him, so that she might clear her name, and his speech would be a proof for her.

In the narration: when she pointed to him, the people became angry and said: "Despite what you have done, you mock and ridicule us!"

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ Then if it is said: What is the meaning of His saying ﴿who is in the cradle, a child﴾, when every man in the world was once a child in the cradle? The answer to this: Abu 'Ubayda said: "kana" is a supplementary (ṣila) particle, and the meaning of the verse is: How can we speak to a child in the cradle? Al-Zajjaj said: This is in the form of a conditional (sharṭ), that is: one who is a child in the cradle, how can we speak to him?

And the meaning of "kana" is: "huwa" (he is), or the meaning of "kana" is: "ṣāra" (became), and this is the preference of Ibn al-Anbari.

The commentary on His words, the Exalted: ﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of God"﴾. In the tafsir (exegesis): when Mary pointed to him, and he was nursing from her breast, he left the breast, turned toward the people, leaned on his left side, gestured with his right hand, and said these words.

His words ﴿Indeed, I am the servant of God﴾ affirm servitude first, lest he be taken as a god.

His words ﴿He has given me the Book﴾ mean the Injil (the Gospel). Most scholars hold that he was given the Injil while still a young child, but they say he understood with the intellect of grown men. This is the view of al-Hasan and others among the early generations (al-salaf). It is also reported from al-Hasan that he said: "He was made a prophet and given the Injil while still in his mother's womb."

Some said: ﴿He has given me the Book﴾ means "He will give me the Book and make me a prophet when I become a man." The first view is the correct one. Some others said: at that time he was described as Adam was, in intellect and knowledge, though not in stature and bodily form.

It is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: His mother entrusted him to a teacher. The teacher said: "Say: Bismi (in the name of)." He said: "Allah." The teacher said: "Say: al-Rahman." He said: "al-Rahim." Whenever the teacher named a word, he would name the one that followed it. The teacher said: "He knows more than I do." Then he began to inform the children about what their mothers had hidden in their houses, so the children would return to their homes and take it, and the mothers cried out about this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 31:

So His saying, ﴿and He has made me blessed﴾, means: a source of benefit (naffa'an), a teacher of good. Al-Dahhak said: one who fulfills needs.

Al-Thawri said: one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong.

His saying, ﴿wherever I may be﴾, means: wherever I am.

His saying, ﴿and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat﴾, means: He has commanded me to pray and to pay zakat. If it is said: Jesus had no wealth, so how could he be commanded to pay zakat? The answer: its meaning is that He commanded me to pay zakat if I had wealth. It has also been said: "He commanded me to pay zakat" means: to purify oneself from sins; and it is said: to increase in good.

His saying, ﴿as long as I remain alive﴾, means: for as long as I live.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning: merciful and kind to my mother.

And His saying: ﴿And He has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾. The jabbar (tyrant) is the arrogant one (al-mutakabbir), and the shaqi (wretched) is the one who disobeys Allah. It is also said: the jabbar is the one who kills and strikes out of anger, and this is a well-known statement. It is also said: the jabbar is the one who wrongs people, and the shaqi is the one who commits sins and does not repent of the sin.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 33:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾. Its meaning: greetings and protection from God for me on the day I was born, ﴿and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾. Some of them said: "Peace" here means safety at birth, which is safety from the prick of Satan and his goading. Safety at death is from shirk, for most shirk occurs at death. And safety on the Day of Resurrection is from its terrors.

It was also said: safety at death from the squeezing of the grave. And it was said: safety at death by arriving at happiness.

That is (ذلك) Jesus son of Mary, meaning: this is Jesus son of Mary. ﴿The word of truth about which they dispute.﴾ Meaning: this statement is the true statement. And His words ﴿about which they dispute﴾ mean: they differ concerning it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not befitting for Allah to take any son﴾. Its meaning: it is not fitting for Allah, and it does not behoot Him, to take a son.

If it is said: why did He not say "a son" (waladan)? We say: He said "any son" (min walad) for emphasis (al-mubalaghah), for a man may say, "So-and-so has not acquired a horse," meaning in number, even though he has acquired one. When he says, "So-and-so has not acquired any horse," that is a negation of the one and of the number. We have already explained that the son is of the same kind as the father, and Allah has no kind.

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of qada' (decree).

And His saying: ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ — we have also mentioned this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord﴾. Most of the exegetes say that this is built upon the saying of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, and its meaning is: He said, "Indeed I am the servant of Allah..." to the end, and he said: "Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord." As for the reading with the fatha (wa-anna, "and that"), its meaning is: and he informed that Allah is my Lord and your Lord. It was also said that its estimated form is: "And because Allah is my Lord and your Lord, worship Him," and the governing element (al-ʿamil) is His saying: ﴿So worship Him﴾.

And His saying: ﴿So worship Him; this is a straight path﴾ is apparent in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾. Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and others said: When ʿIsa (peace be upon him) was raised up to the heaven, the Children of Israel chose four of their leaders and asked them about ʿIsa, and they differed. One of them said: He was God, who descended from the heaven, entered the womb of Maryam, gave life and caused death, then ascended to the heaven. The others said: You have lied. This is the view of the Yaʿqubiyya among the Christians.

The second said: He was the son of God. The other two said: You have lied. This is the view of the Nestorians among the Christians.

The third said: He was the third of three: God, Maryam and ʿIsa. So ʿIsa is one of the three hypostases (aqanim). This is the view of the Melkites among the Christians. The fourth said: You have lied. Then the fourth said: He is the servant of God and His messenger. Each one was followed by a group, and they fought one another, and the [party of the] Muslims prevailed, and the three views among the Christians remained. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾.

His saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve﴾. We have already explained the meaning of woe (al-wayl).

His saying: ﴿From the scene of a tremendous day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection.

"The Most High's saying: ﴿How well they will hear and see [on] the Day they come to Us!﴾ That is: how keen their hearing and seeing will be on the Day of Resurrection. He described them with this because He, exalted is He, had described them in this world as deaf, mute and blind, so He informed that they would hear and see in the Hereafter what they did not hear and see in this world. It is also said: He described them with an intense degree of hearing and sight in the Hereafter, by the occurrence of perception without sight or reflection.

As for His saying: ﴿On the Day they come to Us﴾, its meaning is apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿But the wrongdoers today are in clear error﴾, that is: manifest error.

It is also said that His saying: ﴿How well they will hear and see﴾ is a threat and a warning, and its meaning is: they will hear what splits their hearts, and see what destroys them."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 39:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾ mean: the Day of remorse. It is also said: all people will feel remorse on the Day of Resurrection. The one who did wrong will regret not having done good, and the one who did good will regret not having increased (in good) [ḥusnan]. As for the view of most of the exegetes concerning this verse, that this regret occurs when Death is slaughtered on the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ), the report has been authenticated through the narration of Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:

"When Allah admits the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will raise their heads and look. And he will call out: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will raise their heads and look. Then Death will be brought in the form of a horned ram, white with black spots, and it will be said to them: 'Do you recognize this?' They will say: 'We recognize it; this is Death.' Then it will be slaughtered." In the narration of Abu Hurayrah: "It will be slaughtered on the Ṣirāṭ." Then it will be said: "O people of Paradise, eternity (without death)! And O people of the Fire, eternity, with no death!" In some narrations: "If the people of Paradise were to die, they would die of joy, and if the people of the Fire were to die, they would die of grief." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided﴾ ... the verse.

His words ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾ mean: the matter has been concluded.

His words ﴿while they are heedless﴾ mean: while they are heedless in this world of what will be done to them in the Hereafter.

His words ﴿and they do not believe﴾ mean: they do not affirm (the truth).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, etc. Its meaning: We cause the inhabitants of the earth to die and destroy them, so the earth and whoever is upon it will belong to Us and be under Our command. The meaning of inheritance (al-irth) is that no one remains with any possession or cause other than God.

His saying: ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, i.e., they will be sent back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 41:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.﴾ Al-Siddiq (the one who is truthful) is: one who is abundant in truthfulness, steadfast upon it. It is also said: whoever is truthful toward God in His oneness, and truthful toward His prophets and messengers, and truthful about the Resurrection, and who stands by the commands, acting upon them, is a siddiq.

And His words: ﴿a prophet﴾. The nabi (prophet) is: one elevated in rank by God's sending him, and by the establishment of proof of his truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 19, verse 42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When he said to his father, "O my father"﴾ means: "O my father" (yā abī), and the "tā'" (ت) was put in the place of the "yā'" of possession (yā' al-idāfah).

And His saying: ﴿Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees and cannot benefit you at all?﴾ That is: it does not hear if you call upon it, and it does not see if you come to it. ﴿And cannot benefit you at all﴾ means it cannot ward off anything from you; its meaning is that it cannot relieve you if you seek relief from it.

Almighty God's words: ﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you﴾, that is: of knowledge and recognition of God that has not come to you.

﴿So follow me; I will guide you﴾, guide you ﴿to a path, even and straight﴾, upright.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾. Its meaning: do not obey Satan in what he makes attractive to you of disbelief and polytheism.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to the Most Merciful a disobedient one﴾. That is: ʿaṣiyan (disobedient).

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O my father, indeed I fear﴾. Here, "fear" (al-khawf) carries the meaning of knowledge (al-'ilm). Its meaning is: indeed I know that ﴿a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you﴾ if you persist in disbelief.

﴿Then you would become a friend (waliyy) of Satan﴾. He means: there would be incumbent upon you wilaya, that is, allegiance (muwalat) to Satan, and you would be like him. It has also been said: you would be entrusted (fa-tuwakkalu) to Satan, and Allah would forsake you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 46:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim?﴾

Regarding the story: Ibrahim's father used to carve idols and worship them, and he would give the idols to his sons to sell. Whenever he gave Ibrahim an idol to sell, Ibrahim would say: "Who will buy from me what harms him and does not benefit him?" So he would return without having sold anything, while the rest of the sons would return having sold theirs.

As for His saying: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim?﴾, it is said: "raghiba 'an al-shay'" means he abandoned it when he left it, and "raghiba fi al-shay'" means he sought it (when he desired it).

As for His saying: ﴿If you do not desist﴾, meaning: from your action. ﴿I will surely stone you﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "I will surely kill you with stones." Others said: "I will surely revile you, and I will drive you away from myself with abuse and foul speech." This second view is the better known of the two. As for His saying: ﴿And leave me for a long time (malliyyan)﴾, al-Hasan said: "A long time." 'Ikrimah said: "An age."

Muhalhil said in verse:

(So the solid mountains were split at his death, and the widowed women wept for him for a long time (malliyyan).)

From this comes the phrase "al-mulawan," which means the night and the day. It is also said that "malliyyan" means: safe and sound from my punishment and my harm, and this is reported from Ibn 'Abbas. From the same root: "fulan mulin bi-amr kadhā," meaning he is complete and proficient in that matter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Peace be upon you."﴾

Some of them said: this is a peace of parting and separation. Others said: it is a peace of goodness and gentleness, and it is the reply of the forbearing to the foolish, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾

It is also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿salaman (peace)﴾ is: safety for you from me, because he had not been commanded to fight him.

As for His saying ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord if you believe." The second opinion: "I will ask Allah on your behalf for the repentance that brings about forgiveness," and his repentance was indeed faith. As for His saying ﴿Indeed, He has been ever gracious to me﴾, it means: He has made my supplications answered for me, habitually. It was also said: "affectionate" (muhibban).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 48:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿And I will withdraw from you﴾: this withdrawal [is] his leaving them when he emigrated to al-Sham, as He said in another place: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord"﴾.

And His words, ﴿and what you invoke other than Allah﴾: that is, what you worship other than Allah.

And His words, ﴿and I will invoke my Lord﴾: that is, I will worship my Lord.

And His words, ﴿perhaps I will not be in my invocation to my Lord [as] one unblessed﴾: "perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is obligatory; and "invocation" (duʿāʾ) means worship; and "unblessedness" (shaqāwa) is deprivation of mercy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 49:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾ ﴿and Jacob﴾ — he is the son of Isaac.

Its meaning: We gave him children, noble and dutiful, in exchange for those whom he used to call to the worship of Allah but who did not respond.

As for His words: ﴿And each We made a prophet﴾, He means: Isaac and Jacob.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 50:

﴿And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy﴾ means: We blessed them, and gave them of Our honor and Our favors.

And His saying: ﴿And We granted them a tongue of truthfulness, high and exalted﴾ means: a good praise until the Day of Resurrection. And we have already explained that all the people of the religions speak well of Ibrahim, so he is the good praise until the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 51:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Moses; indeed he was sincere (mukhlaṣan)﴾. It is read "mukhlaṣan" and "mukhlaṣan" with a fatḥa and with a kasra. With the kasra, meaning: one who affirms the oneness of God (muwaḥḥidan li-Llah); and with the fatḥa, meaning: one chosen (mukhtāran) by God the Exalted. It is also said: mukhlaṣan means khāliṣan (purified, pure), and this is like the words of the Exalted: ﴿a man belonging wholly to one master (rajulan salaman li-rajul)﴾, meaning: purely belonging to one man.

And His words: ﴿and he was a messenger (rasūlan), a prophet (nabiyyan)﴾. It has been said: the messenger (rasūl) and the prophet (nabī) are one and the same, and it has been said that they are distinguished, and we have explained this before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 52:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount (al-Tur)﴾. Al-Tur: a mountain between Egypt and Madyan. It is said that its name is al-Zubayr.

And His words: ﴿al-Ayman (the right)﴾. It is said: the right side of the mountain. It is also said: the right side of Musa. The more sound view is the right side of Musa, because the mountain has no right or left.

And His words: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He brought him close until he heard the scratching of the pen. It is also said: the scraping of the pen. In another narration: He raised him above the veils.

It is said: "We brought him near (qarrabnahu) as a confidant (najiyyan)" means: We spoke to him. Here the drawing near (al-taqrib) is speaking (al-takallum). As for al-najiy, it is the one who converses in secret (al-munajiy). The meaning according to this view seems to be: Allah speaks to him, and he speaks to Allah.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾. The people of tafsir said: He called Harun's prophethood a gift (hibah) to Musa only because Musa had said: ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 54:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Ismail﴾. Most scholars hold that this is Ismail son of Ibrahim, father of the Prophet (ﷺ). Some said he is Ismail son of Hizqil, another prophet, since Ismail son of Ibrahim died before Ibrahim. The correct view is the first, for he was sent to Jurhum, a tribe. As for the claim that his death preceded Ibrahim's, it is not known.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾. Sufyan said: God did not promise anything of Himself except that He fulfilled it. It is well known that he promised a person something and waited for him in one place for three days, and so he was called "true to his promise." It is also said: he waited for him for a year.

And from Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: Lying has branches, and the greatest of lying is breaking promises and accusing the innocent.

And in some reports: "The Prophet (ﷺ) made a pact with a man before the revelation. That man said to him, 'Wait for me here, O Muhammad, until I return to you.' He went off and forgot. Then he passed by that place after three days and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting there. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, 'You have tired me, O man; I have been waiting for you since three days ago.'"

And it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he made breaking a promise one third of hypocrisy.

And from Zayd ibn Arqam: whoever promises a person while intending to fulfil it, but then fulfilment does not happen, he does not fall under this threat.

And Qubath ibn Ashyam narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A promise is a gift." This is a gharib (rare) report.

As for His saying: ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾, we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 55:

His saying: ﴿And he used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakat﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And he used to enjoin on his people prayer."

The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: The meaning of His saying ﴿And he used to enjoin on his family﴾ is: his community (ummah). Indeed, the family (ahl) of every prophet is his community.

And His saying ﴿and he was with his Lord well-pleasing﴾ means: chosen (mukhtaran). Its meaning is: God was pleased with him for His prophethood and His messengership.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 56:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾. It has been said: Idris is the grandfather of Nuh (Noah). He was called Idris because of how much he studied the books (durus).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He was the first to write with the pen (qalam), the first to wear clothes, whereas those before him used to wear hides, and the first to take up weapons and fight the disbelievers.

His words: ﴿Indeed, he was truthful, a prophet﴾ — we have already explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 57:

And His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾ has been established by the narration of Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw Idris on the night of the Mi'raj in the fourth heaven." Thus His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾ refers to the raising of him to Paradise, meaning: his elevation.

It has also been said: it is an elevation in rank through loftiness of status. There is disagreement as to whether he, in the fourth heaven, is alive or dead. One of the two opinions is that he is alive.

Some people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said: four of the prophets are living, two in the heaven and two on the earth. As for the two in the heaven: Idris and 'Isa. As for the two on the earth: al-Khidr and Ilyas.

The second opinion is that Idris is dead. Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar) said: Idris had a friend among the angels, who said to him: "I wish to know when I will die, so that I may increase in good deeds. Would you ask the Angel of Death?" He said: "I will ask him while you listen." Then he raised him beneath his wing to the heaven, and came to the Angel of Death and said: "Do you know when Idris will die?" He said: "Let me look." Then he brought out a book, looked into it, and said: "Six hours remain of his life," and in another narration, "a moment." Then he took his soul right there. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾. This is a well-known opinion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 58:

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favour from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam﴾. What is meant by "the descendants of Adam" is Idris.

His saying: ﴿And of those whom We carried with Nuh﴾. That is: and of the descendants of those whom We carried with Nuh. What is meant by them is Ibrahim, because he was from the lineage of Sam ibn Nuh.

His saying: ﴿And of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾. What is meant by them is Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Isra'il﴾. That is: of the descendants of Isra'il. What is meant by them is Musa, Dawud, Sulayman, Yusuf and Isa, and all the prophets of the Children of Isra'il.

His saying: ﴿And of those whom We guided and chose﴾. This refers back to the first group, and its meaning is: We guided them and selected them, and these are their descendants.

His saying: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping﴾. That is: they fell down. It has been said: they fell upon their faces prostrating. The word "sujjad" is the plural of "sajid" (one who prostrates).

His saying: ﴿and weeping﴾. That is: weeping.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a man who was prostrating and supplicating, and he said: "This is prostration, but where is the weeping?!"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 59:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾. Al-khalf (a later generation, successors): the bad ones of the people. And al-khalf al-salih (the righteous successor) among the people. And al-khalf is the one who succeeds another. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj mentioned that it is permissible to use either of them in place of the other.

And His words: ﴿They neglected the prayer﴾. Concerning this there are two views. The first: they delayed it past its time. The second: they abandoned it altogether. It is related from Ibn Shawdhab: it is the delaying of it beyond its time, and if they had abandoned it altogether, they would have disbelieved.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: it is their drinking of wine and their abandonment of the prayer.

Mujahid said: these are a people who will appear at the end of time, leaping upon one another in the markets and the alleys. It was also said: they are the fornicators. And it is said: they neglected the prayer by following their desires.

And His words: ﴿So they will meet error (ghayy)﴾. It was said: al-ghayy is a valley in Hell. It was said: ghayy means destruction. It was said: ghayy means the recompense of their error (ghayy). Poetry:

(Whoever meets good, people will praise his affair... and whoever goes astray will not lack a blamer for his error.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 60:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds; those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.﴾ That is, they will not be deprived of anything (of their reward).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 61:

His saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants in the unseen﴾. Its meaning: gardens of residence (iqamah). It is said: "adan bil-makan" (ʿadana), when he resided in the place.

And His saying: ﴿which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants in the unseen﴾, meaning: in the hidden (al-maghyib).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled (ma'tiyyan)﴾. It is a maf'ul (passive participle) from al-iti'an (coming/arriving), and everything that you have come to has come to you. The Arabs do not distinguish between one who says "ataytu ʿala khamsin sanah" (I have reached fifty years) and one who says "atat ʿala khamsuna sanah" (fifty years have come upon him), and likewise they do not distinguish between one who says "wasala al-khayru ilayya" (the good reached me) and one who says "wasala ilayya al-khayr" (the good reached me).

It is said that the meaning of His saying "ma'tiyyan" (ātiyan) is "ma'tiyyan," meaning a maf'ul in the sense of a fa'il (active participle).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 62:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain talk, but only "Peace."﴾

Al-laghw: it is corrupt speech and that which has no meaning. It was also said: it is idle talk. It was also said: it is ugly speech from it. It was also said: it is false oaths.

As for His words ﴿but only "Peace"﴾, its meaning is: rather, they will hear "Peace." If it is said: is it permissible to make "peace" an exception from "vain talk," when it is not of its kind? We say: it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), as we have explained. Al-Azhari mentioned that its implied sense is: "They will not hear therein vain talk; they will hear nothing but peace." As for al-salam (peace), it is the greeting of some of them to others. It was also said: it is the greeting of Allah upon them. And it is said: it is a word from which one is safe. Al-Salam is a name for a comprehensive speech that gathers all goodness, and some have said: it is a name for speech connected with safety.

As for His words ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾: if it is asked, what is the meaning of His words "morning and evening," when there is neither night nor day in Paradise? The answer to this is that its meaning is: morning and evening-time, that is, according to the measures of mornings and evenings.

It is also said: they know the time of day by the raising of the veils and the opening of the doors, and the time of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors.

The second opinion: the meaning of His words "morning and evening" is that they will have therein the ease of living, abundant provision without restriction or scarcity.

When al-Hasan al-Basri recited this verse, he would say: The Arabs have indeed known that the most luxurious living is provision in the morning and the evening, and they do not recognize any luxury beyond this.

That is the Paradise which We cause to be inherited by those of Our servants who were God-fearing (taqi).

Concerning His words, "That is the Paradise which We cause to be inherited from among Our servants," there are two opinions. The first: it is given and granted (as a gift). The other opinion: there is no one among the disbelievers except that he has a dwelling in Paradise, and his people would have it had he embraced Islam; so when he does not embrace Islam, the believers inherit it.

And His words, "Whoever was God-fearing (taqiyyan)," it has been said: sincere (mukhlisan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 64:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾. It is established through the narration of ʿUmar ibn Dhar, from his father, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that Jibril (Gabriel) delayed coming to the Prophet. When he descended, he said: "O Jibril, would that you visited us more often than you do." So Jibril said: "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord."

In some narrations, the Prophet said to him: "O Jibril, I have been longing for you." (He said: "O Muhammad, by God, I too have been longing for you.") "But we do not descend except by the command of your Lord."

It is also related that he delayed twelve nights, and it is related that it was more than this, and God knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us﴾. That is, to Him belongs the knowledge of what is before us and what is behind us. There are several opinions regarding the verse:

The first: "What is before us" refers to the Hereafter, "what is behind us" refers to what has passed of the world, and "what is between that" is from the Hour until the blast of the Trumpet.

The second opinion: "What is before us" is what we face and confront, and "what is behind us" is what we turn our backs on and leave behind; "between that" is the present time and state.

The third opinion: "What is before us" is the earth, "what is behind us" is the heavens, and "what is between that" is the air.

The fourth opinion: "What is before us" is after we die, "what is behind us" is before we were created, and "what is between that" is the duration of life.

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is never forgetful﴾. That is, your Lord has not forgotten you, and the meaning of "forgotten you" is: abandoned you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 65:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾: its meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿So worship Him﴾, meaning: alone.

And His saying: ﴿And be patient in His worship﴾, meaning: be steadfast in worshipping Him.

And His saying: ﴿Do you know anyone worthy of His name?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Do you know anyone named "al-Rahman" other than God? It was also said: anyone named "Allah" other than God. Qatada said: ﴿Do you know anyone worthy of His name?﴾, meaning: an equal. Some of them said: "samiyyan" means: a son.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 19, verse 66:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, shall I then be brought forth alive?"﴾ They said: the verse was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

And His saying: ﴿Shall I indeed be brought forth alive?﴾ That is: "Shall I be brought forth alive?"

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Does not man remember?﴾ Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "Does not man reflect (yatadhakkar al-insan)?" Its meaning: does he not reflect and consider? ﴿man﴾.

And His saying: ﴿We created him before, when he was nothing.﴾ Its meaning: since We were able to bring them into being at their creation, We are all the more able to bring them back (to life)."

The Most High's saying: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely gather them, and the devils.﴾ In a report, every disbeliever will be gathered chained together (musalsalan) with a devil.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, on their knees.﴾ That is, kneeling (jathin) on their knees. Al-Suddi said: "Sitting on their knees because of the narrowness of the place." "Around Hell" is Hell itself.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We will certainly drag out from every sect﴾, meaning: We will certainly extract and seize from every sect, that is, from every community and people of religion among the disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will certainly know best who is most deserving of burning therein﴾ (the verse as rendered here), meaning: those who are most rebellious first, and the meaning of the verse is: We shall advance in entering the Fire those who are greater in sin and more severe in matter. The people of linguistic expertise (ahl al-lughah) said: His saying ﴿ʿitiyyan﴾ means "falsehood" (iftira') in the dialect of Tamim. It is said: "These are the leaders of disbelief and its chiefs." In some reports it is mentioned that they will all be brought around Hell, shackled in chains, and then the most disbelieving among them will be brought forward, then the next most disbelieving.

Almighty God's words: ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein.﴾ That is, most deserving of entering it. And it is said: "Those who are most obstinate are most deserving of burning therein," and this is the interpretation of the verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ means: "And there is none of you but will pass over it." The scholars differed as to what the pronoun in His saying ﴿it﴾ refers back to. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the Fire. He said: al-wurud (coming to, passing over) is entering. He said: the righteous and the wicked will all enter it, then the righteous will be saved and the wicked will remain.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: Ibn 'Abbas and Nafi' ibn al-Azraq disputed about al-wurud. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is entering. He recited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be arriving at it﴾. Then he said: "O Nafi', I and you will both enter it. I hope that Allah will save me from it, and He will not save you from it, because you denied it."

The Shaykh, the Imam, the most venerable Abu al-Muzaffar al-Sam'ani said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us in Mecca, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn [Furas] informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muqri' informed us, saying: my grandfather Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us from Sufyan.

Qurrah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that people will come to the Fire, and the believers will leave it by their deeds: the first of them like the blink of an eye, then like the wind, then like the galloping of a horse, then like the running of a man, then like the walking of a man.

And from Ibn Maysara, that he used to enter his house and weep. He was asked: "What makes you weep?" He would say: "Allah, may He be exalted, has informed us that we will come to the Fire, and He has not informed us that we will depart from it."

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "It is right for the son of Adam to weep..." and he mentioned something similar to this.

The second view: the intended meaning of the verse is the disbelievers. This is the view of 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It is read in the irregular reading: ﴿And there is none of them but will pass over it﴾. Many scholars hold this view, and they cited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, they will be kept far away from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾.

The third view: the intended meaning of al-wurud is presence and sight, not entering. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and al-wurud is sometimes used in the sense of presence. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when he came to the water of Madyan﴾, meaning: arrived at it. Zuhayr said in verse:

(When they came to the water, its pools blue-black, they left the staves of the one who stays and encamps.)

The fourth view, which is related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ refers to the Resurrection. They have deemed this view preferable because the Resurrection was mentioned earlier.

The fifth view: that it refers to the Sirat (the bridge over Hell).

In the verse there is a sixth view: it is narrated from Mujahid that he said: the coming to the Fire is the fever in this world.

In some collections of hadith it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he visited a man suffering from fever (wa'k, i.e. the fever) and said: "Allah, may He be exalted, says: It is My Fire; I impose it upon whomever I wish of the believers, so that its share for him is from the Fire of Hell."

In some reports: "Fever is an expiation (kiyy) from Hell, and it is the believer's share of the Fire."

It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Fever is from the heat (fayh) of Hell, so cool it with water."

The most preferable of these sayings is the first view, and it is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever of his children dies before puberty will not enter the Fire, except for the fulfilment of the oath (tahillat al-qasam)."

In some reports: "It (the Fire) blazes against the disbelievers and is extinguished under the feet of the believers."

Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah will admit some of the believers into Paradise, and they will say: 'Did You not promise us, our Lord, that we would enter the Fire?' He will say to them: 'You have passed over it while it was extinguished.'"

His saying: ﴿It is a decree decided by your Lord﴾, meaning: an obligatory matter that must befall.

Almost fully translated; here is the passage:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall save those who had taward God-consciousness﴾ Those who said that "wurud" (coming to it) means entering took this as evidence, because deliverance (tanjiyah) only occurs after entering. He also said: ﴿And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein, kneeling﴾, and this is evidence that all of them have entered it. As for those who said that "wurud" means being present (al-hudur), they said: it is permissible to mention deliverance because of having come near to destruction.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾ means: clear, evident.

And His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Which of the two groups is better in station (maqam)?"﴾ means: in place (makan). And His saying: ﴿and better in assembly (nadiyy)﴾ — Tha'lab said: "a gathering (majlis)." Al-Kisa'i said: "al-nadiyy and al-nadi (the assembly) have the same meaning, and from it comes Dar al-Nadwa (the House of Assembly), because they used to gather in it."

The occasion of revelation of the verse: the polytheists used to say to the poor among the believers, "We are more honoured in gathering, better in place, and greater in wealth." So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse. Al-Maqam (the station) is the place of residing, and al-maqam is also the act of residing. The poet said:

(A noble station, whose owner separated... by my sword, my tongue and my debate)

(If the elephant or its like were to... slip away from a station like my station and depart)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were better in equipment and in appearance (ri'yan)?﴾ It is also recited as "wiryan" (ريا) without a hamza, and in the irregular (shadhdh) reading as "ziyyan" (وزيا) with a zay. This is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. As for His saying ﴿ri'yan﴾ with the hamza, it means the appearance (al-manzara). As for the reading without the hamza, it means blessing (al-ni'mah). As for az-zayy, it means the outward form (al-hay'ah). It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: [And better in ri'yan] means beauty of form. It was also said: ar-Ri halways from irtiwa' (quenching/satiety), and the one who lives in luxury shows in himself the satiety of blessing, while the poor person shows upon himself the wilting of misery and poverty.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension﴾. This is a command that carries the meaning of a report. Its meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, leaves them in disbelief and gives them respite in it.

And His saying: ﴿until, when they see that which they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour﴾. The punishment (al-'adhab) is killing and capture in this world, and the Hour (al-sa'ah) is the Resurrection. Its meaning: if the believers are granted victory over them in this world, so that they are killed and taken captive, or the Hour comes upon them and they are made to enter the Fire, ﴿then they will know﴾ at that time ﴿who is worse in position﴾, that is, in dwelling, ﴿and weaker in forces﴾, that is, in helpers.

And His saying: ﴿and weaker in forces﴾ refers to the world, and His saying: ﴿worse in position﴾ refers to the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 76:

﴿And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance﴾. He means: certainty upon their certainty, and right guidance upon their right guidance.

And His saying: ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾. It has been said: they are the five daily prayers. And it has been said: they are the remembrances (adhkar) which we have mentioned, and we have already explained them.

And His saying: ﴿Better in reward with your Lord﴾, meaning: in recompense, ﴿and better in return﴾, meaning: in outcome/place of return. Al-Kalbi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas [that] the increase in guidance is faith in the abrogating and the abrogated (al-nasikh wa'l-mansukh).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 19, verse 77:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse is what Masruq narrated from Khabbab [ibn] al-Aratt, who said: "I was a smith and blacksmith in Makkah, and I worked for al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and dirhams accumulated for me upon him. So I came to him demanding my payment, and he said, 'I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' I said, 'I will not disbelieve until you die and are then resurrected.' Al-'As said, 'Or shall I be resurrected?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'When I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children there, and then I will pay you your due?' So Allah the Most High revealed this verse."

The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This was informed to us by al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq, who said: Our grandfather Abu al-Layth informed us, who said: al-Firabri said: al-Bukhari narrated to us, who said: al-Humaydi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq ... the hadith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 78:

And His saying: ﴿Has he looked into the unseen?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). It was also said: the knowledge of the unseen. So does he know that he will have wealth and children through knowledge of the unseen?

And His saying: ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ Sufyan said: a righteous deed. Others said: "There is no god but Allah."

Al-Aswad ibn Yazid narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection, Allah, exalted is He, will say: 'Whoever has a covenant with Me, let him stand.'" It was asked: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, what is that covenant? Teach us." He said: He said: "Is one of you unable to make for himself a covenant every morning and evening? They said: 'How?' He said: He says: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I take a covenant with You in this worldly life, and if You leave me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good, and I trust in nothing but Your mercy. So guard my covenant and return it to me on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not break the promise.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 79:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay! We shall record what he says﴾. His saying: ﴿Nay!﴾ means: the matter is not as al-As ibn Wa'il claimed. Then He said: ﴿We shall record what he says﴾, meaning: He commands the angels so that they write it down.

And His saying: ﴿And We shall extend for him the extension of punishment﴾, meaning: We shall prolong the duration of his punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 80:

And His saying: ﴿And We shall inherit from him what he says﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and We shall inherit from him what is with him." If it is said: how can speech be inherited, when the well-known reading is ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾? The answer to this was given by Tha'lab, who said: its meaning is: We shall inherit from him what he claimed he had of wealth and offspring; that is, We will not give it to him, but give it to another. So the inheritance refers to what lies beneath the speech, not to the speech itself.

It is also permissible that the meaning of His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾ is: and We shall inherit from him what is with him, in accordance with what Ibn Mas'ud recited.

There is a third view regarding the verse, which is that the meaning of His saying ﴿and We shall inherit from him what he says﴾ is: We preserve what he says until he is recompensed for it.

And His saying: ﴿And he will come to Us alone﴾, meaning: alone, with no helpers or supporters. It was also said that it has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [6:94]. Its real meaning is that he will come to Us with no wealth and no offspring.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an, Qur'anic exegesis)**

His, the Exalted's, statement: ﴿And they have taken gods besides God﴾ means: gods that they worship.

And His statement: ﴿that they may be for them a source of ʿizz﴾, that is, مَنْعَة (manʿah, protection). The meaning of manʿah is that they seek protection through them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 82:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay⁠—﴾ meaning: the matter is not as they claimed.

And His saying: ﴿They will deny their worship of them﴾ has two interpretations. One: the idols and the angels will deny their worship. The other: the polytheists will deny the worship of the idols and the angels.

If it is said: Was there any known polytheist who worshipped the angels? We say: That is not so. There was a clan of the Arabs called Banu al-Mulayh, who worshipped the angels.

And His saying: ﴿And they will be to them adversaries﴾ means: a calamity. It was also said: enemies.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 83:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers?﴾ If it is said: Do you say that the devils are "sent" (mursalun), while God said: ﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾? So if they are "sent," they must be included among them? The answer to this: the meaning of "sending" (al-irsal) here is not the sending that is found in the prophets, but the meaning of "sending" here is one of two things: either leaving them free (al-takhliyah) between them and the disbelievers, or empowering them (al-taslit) over the disbelievers.

And His words: ﴿urging them with urging﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Driving them with a driving; as if it were stirring them and inciting them and saying: Advance into disbelief." And al-hazz and al-azz are: stirring. And in the report: "that the Prophet (ﷺ) was praying, and in his chest there was a rumbling like the rumbling of a cauldron (al-mirjal)," meaning: a movement.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 84:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So do not hasten against them﴾ mean: do not hasten to seek their punishment.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We are counting for them a counting﴾. Al-Kalbi said: it is the counting of the days. Others said: it is the counting of the hours.

It is narrated from al-Hasan: it is the counting of the breaths. It was said to one of the righteous people: "Your days are only counted breaths," and he said: "I fear for the accuracy of the count."

al-Asma'i narrated from his father that he said: "I saw a man at the gate of Basra during the time of the plague counting the dead, and in front of him was a jug. Every time a dead person passed by him, he would throw a pebble into it. On the first day he counted eighty thousand, and on the second day one hundred and twenty thousand." He said: "We passed by him with a funeral, then we returned, and beside the jug there was someone else. We said to him: 'Where has the man gone?' He said: 'He fell into the jug.'"

The Almighty said: ﴿On the Day when We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾. Al-hashr (gathering): bringing together the peoples from every region into one place.

As for His words ﴿wafdan﴾ (as a delegation), its meaning is: riding (on mounts).
