It is reported from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited this verse and said: They will be brought with she-camels of the camels of Paradise, upon which are saddles of gold, and whose reins are of chrysolite (zabarjad), and they will ride them until they knock at the gate of Paradise. And in some reports from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "The Prophets will be gathered on mounts in Paradise, and I will be gathered on the Buraq, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn will be gathered on al-ʿAdbaʾ and al-Qaswaʾ, and Bilal will be gathered on a she-camel of the camels of Paradise, and he will call the adhan. Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 87:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They will not have the power of intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾. Some of the people of tafsir said: this refers to the angels. Others said: it refers to the believers.

As for His words: ﴿except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾, it means: they will not intercede except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful. The covenant is "there is no god but Allah." And it is said: none will intercede except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning: none will intercede except a believer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 90:

Allah's statement: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it﴾. Infitar (infitār) means splitting open (inshiqaq), and takadu (تكاد) means "nearly" or "approach." In the exegesis it is related that when the disbelievers said, "Allah has taken a son," the heavens and the earth became angry, and Hell was kindled, so all of them sought to take vengeance upon those who spoke this statement. This is the meaning of the verse.

His statement: ﴿And the earth is split asunder﴾ means it sinks them into the ground. As for the splitting (infitar) in the sky, its meaning according to this is that it [falls] upon them.

His statement: ﴿And the mountains fall down in ruin﴾ means they are broken into pieces, and its meaning according to what we have mentioned is that they crush them.

The scholars have unanimously agreed that sonship and servitude (ʿubudiyyah) cannot be combined, and whoever buys his son, he is freed upon him, because he is not suitable to be both a son and a slave.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 96:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ — meaning: love (mahabbah). Mujahid said: Allah loves them, and makes them beloved to the believers. It was also said: they love one another. And in some reports it is related that Allah, exalted is He, has joined with faith love, [compassion] and affinity.

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), via the narration of Abu Hurairah, that he said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'I love so-and-so, so love him.' Then Jibril calls out among the inhabitants of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' Then the inhabitants of the heavens love him, and then acceptance (al-qabul) is placed for him on the earth — and in another narration, 'love' is placed for him on the earth. And when He hates a servant, Jibril calls out and says: 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' Then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' Then hatred is placed for him on the earth." Related by Muslim in his Sahih.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas that the verse was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and what is meant by it is the affection of the people of faith for him.

It has also been narrated from the Prophet that he said to 'Ali: "None loves you except a believing, pious person, and none hates you except a hypocrite, wretched one." Related by Muslim in his Sahih.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾, meaning: We have made the Qur'an easy by means of your tongue.

And His saying: ﴿that you may give glad tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people given to contention﴾. Ludd is the plural of alladd (the most contentious), and alladd is one who disputes in falsehood. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is the one who does not submit to the truth and does not accept it. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ludda means deaf to the truth. It has also been said: alladd here is the wrongdoer. The poet said:

(I pass the night in private grief, as though I were ... disputing with people who are full of contention, ludda)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 19, verse 98:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them. Do you perceive any one of them, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾ Its meaning: "Do you see any one of them?"

And His words: ﴿or hear from them a faint sound﴾, meaning: a sound. The people of the lexicon (ahl al-lughah) said: al-rikz (the faint sound) is a hidden sound. al-Hasan said: they all perished, so no trace or sign of them remained.
